decode.needs: Classic view mobile best practice: new browser tab, not iframe
clues: payment field -> classic view is required
phones, cramped iframe -> open in a new tab on mobile
pricing tiers -> red herring

concept.title: Classic view on mobile
concept.line: In classic view let Docusign take the full window; on mobile browsers open a new tab instead of an iframe.

stem: Which request returns the URL for an embedded sending session on a draft envelope?

options.text: POST .../envelopes/{envelopeId}/views/sender
POST .../envelopes/{envelopeId}/views/recipient
POST .../envelopes/{envelopeId}/views/correct
PUT .../envelopes/{envelopeId} with status sent

answerText: POST .../envelopes/{envelopeId}/views/sender
explanation: Embedded sending uses EnvelopeViews:createSender, POST .../envelopes/{envelopeId}/views/sender, on a draft envelope.
whyNotOthers: A is right. The trap is C: the correct view is also a sender-side view, but for envelopes already sent. B is for signers and D sends without UI.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. This is EnvelopeViews:createSender.
optionExplanations.B: This returns a signing URL for a recipient.
optionExplanations.C: This returns the correction view for an envelope already sent.
optionExplanations.D: This sends the draft directly, with no sending UI.

concept.title: Embedded sending endpoint
concept.line: views/sender embeds tagging and sending of a draft; views/recipient embeds signing; views/correct embeds correction.

stem: Orbis Streaming wants new subscribers to accept updated terms of service inside its web app with a single 'I agree' button. Legal wants the acceptance captured in Docusign with a full audit trail, but there is nothing for the subscriber to type, initial or sign. The product team wants the experience to blend into the app's design. The terms are updated twice a year. How should the integration present the terms?

options.text: Create the envelope with the subscriber as an embedded recipient with no fields, and show it with classic view in an iframe so the full signing toolbar is available
Add a single checkbox field labelled I agree for the subscriber and show it with classic view
Send the terms to the subscriber as a carbon copy recipient so they can read them by email
Create the envelope with the subscriber as an embedded recipient with no fields, and show it with focused view, which falls back to a click-to-agree experience

answerText: Create the envelope with the subscriber as an embedded recipient with no fields, and show it with focused view, which falls back to a click-to-agree experience
explanation: With focused view, an envelope that has no fields for the recipient is shown as a click-to-agree experience, and focused view blends into the app.
whyNotOthers: D is right. The trap is A: same envelope, wrong view; click-to-agree fallback is listed as a focused view benefit. B adds a field and the full UI, and C records no acceptance.

optionExplanations.A: Classic view shows the full Docusign signing interface; the automatic click-to-agree fallback is a focused view feature.
optionExplanations.B: This forces a field and the full classic UI, which the product team wanted to avoid.
optionExplanations.C: A carbon copy captures no acceptance.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Focused view with no tabs for the recipient automatically becomes a clickwrap-style agreement with an agree button.

decode.needs: Focused view + recipient with no tabs = click-to-agree
clues: single I agree button, nothing to type or sign -> no tabs
blend into the app's design -> focused view
updated twice a year -> red herring

concept.title: Focused view click-to-agree
concept.line: In focused view a recipient with no fields gets a clickwrap-style agree button automatically.

stem: Riverbend Insurance's claims portal lets a claimant start signing a settlement, leave, and come back days later to finish from the portal. The portal must be able to open a fresh signing session for the same envelope when the claimant returns. Claimants always come back through the portal, never through an email link. The claims database runs on a managed SQL service. Which two values should the portal store for each claimant when it creates the envelope? (Select two)

options.text: The envelopeId returned by Envelopes:create
The signing URL from the first createRecipient call, so the claimant can reopen it
The access token used to create the envelope, so the session can be resumed with it
The returnUrl event received when the claimant left
The clientUserId used for the claimant's recipient

answerText: The envelopeId returned by Envelopes:create; The clientUserId used for the claimant's recipient
explanation: Docusign's best practices say to store the envelope ID for each customer and cache the clientUserId sent for each recipient; the signing URL is requested only when the user is ready.
whyNotOthers: A and E are right. The trap is B: it seems convenient to save the URL, but it expires within minutes and works once. C expires as well, and D is not an input to createRecipient.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. The envelope ID is needed for later calls such as createRecipient.
optionExplanations.B: Signing URLs are short-lived and single-use; request a new one when the claimant returns.
optionExplanations.C: Tokens expire; the app gets a current token when it needs one.
optionExplanations.D: The event is useful for routing the user, but it is not needed to reopen the session.
optionExplanations.E: Correct. createRecipient must repeat the same clientUserId, so cache it per recipient.

decode.needs: Persist envelopeId and clientUserId; request a new recipient view on return
clues: come back days later -> new signing URL needed
fresh session for the same envelope -> envelopeId + matching clientUserId
managed SQL service -> red herring

concept.title: Persist IDs, not URLs
concept.line: Store the envelopeId and each recipient's clientUserId; generate a new signing URL whenever the user is ready to sign.

stem: Marlow Realty's agent portal already lets agents sign and send specific documents. Agents now want to open their full Docusign workspace inside the portal, to browse their inbox and sent items, check statuses and use templates, without logging in to a separate site. Each agent has a Docusign user in the brokerage account, and the portal authenticates them with Authorization Code Grant. The portal was recently redesigned. Which call should the portal use?

options.text: EnvelopeViews:createSender on a new draft envelope, so the agent sees the Docusign sending screen
EnvelopeViews:createConsole, opening the returned URL for the signed-in agent
EnvelopeViews:createRecipient with the agent's clientUserId
EnvelopeViews:createCorrect for the agent's most recent envelope

answerText: EnvelopeViews:createConsole, opening the returned URL for the signed-in agent
explanation: To embed the whole Docusign web app (inbox, sent items, templates) for a user, use the console view, EnvelopeViews:createConsole.
whyNotOthers: B is right. The trap is A: the sender view is the closest embedded view, but it covers one draft envelope. C and D are also single-envelope views.

optionExplanations.A: The sender view is limited to preparing and sending one draft envelope, not the full workspace.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. The console view embeds the Docusign web app for the authenticated user.
optionExplanations.C: The recipient view is a signing session for one envelope.
optionExplanations.D: The correct view edits one sent envelope.

decode.needs: Embedded console view: EnvelopeViews:createConsole
clues: full Docusign workspace, inbox, sent items, templates -> console view
each agent is a Docusign user -> session for the authenticated user
portal recently redesigned -> red herring

concept.title: Embedded console view
concept.line: createConsole embeds the whole web app for a user; createSender, createRecipient and createCorrect each target one envelope.

stem: What does BulkSend:getBulkSendBatchStatus return for a batch?

options.text: Counts of sent, queued and failed envelopes, plus any error messages
The canBeSent flag showing whether the list and envelope are compatible
The listId and the bulk copies stored in the list
The signed documents of every envelope in the batch

answerText: Counts of sent, queued and failed envelopes, plus any error messages
explanation: Checking a bulk send with the batchId returns counts of sent, queued and failed envelopes, as well as error messages.
whyNotOthers: A is right. The trap is B: it is the response of the optional test step, not the status check. C and D belong to other calls.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. The batch status reports sent, queued and failed counts and errors.
optionExplanations.B: canBeSent comes from createBulkSendTestRequest.
optionExplanations.C: These come from the bulk send list endpoints.
optionExplanations.D: Documents are downloaded per envelope.

concept.title: Bulk send return values
concept.line: List returns listId; test returns canBeSent; send returns batchId; batch status returns sent, queued and failed counts.

topic: Bulk send: v2.1 model vs legacy v2
stem: Ironwood College inherited a scholarship-renewal integration written against eSignature REST API v2, which sends one agreement to each of several hundred students by attaching a bulk recipients file to the envelope. The team is moving the integration to v2.1 and wants to follow the current bulk send model. The financial aid office also wants the emails to come from a shared mailbox. Where does the list of students go in v2.1?

options.text: Into a bulk recipients CSV file attached to the envelope's signer, as before, because v2.1 still reads it
Into a bulk send list created with BulkSend:createBulkSendList, whose copies hold each student's recipient details
Into the templateRoles array of one envelope, one entry per student
Into an eventNotification object, so Connect delivers a copy to each student

answerText: Into a bulk send list created with BulkSend:createBulkSendList, whose copies hold each student's recipient details
explanation: Bulk send in v2.1 uses BulkSend resources: create a bulk send list with copies, then send it against a draft envelope or template. The v2 BulkEnvelopes model is legacy.
whyNotOthers: B is right. The trap is A: it describes the v2 approach the team is leaving. C creates one shared envelope and D misuses Connect.

optionExplanations.A: That is the legacy v2 BulkEnvelopes approach; v2.1 changed the construction model to bulk send lists.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. In v2.1 the recipients for each copy are stored in a bulk send list, then sent with createBulkSendRequest.
optionExplanations.C: That would put every student on one envelope.
optionExplanations.D: eventNotification configures webhooks, not recipients.

decode.needs: v2.1 bulk send list (BulkSend:createBulkSendList)
clues: written against v2 with a bulk recipients file -> legacy BulkEnvelopes
moving to v2.1 current model -> bulk send lists
shared mailbox -> red herring

concept.title: Bulk send in v2.1
concept.line: v2.1 bulk send stores recipients in bulk send lists; the v2 BulkEnvelopes resource is the legacy model.

stem: Calloway Legal's matter system stores engagement terms as Word (.docx) files. A developer proposes building a conversion service that turns each file into a PDF before sending it for signature with the direct documents model, which will take two sprints. The partners want the agreements sent next week, the matter system already exports each file as bytes, and the files contain anchor text for the signature lines. What should the lead developer recommend?

options.text: Build the conversion service first, because the eSignature API accepts only PDF documents
Upload each .docx file as a server template by hand and then send it with the template reference model
Send the .docx files as base64, but replace the anchor tabs with fixed x/y positions, because anchors only work in PDFs
Send the .docx files as base64 documents with fileExtension docx, since Docusign accepts DOCX, and keep the anchor tabs

answerText: Send the .docx files as base64 documents with fileExtension docx, since Docusign accepts DOCX, and keep the anchor tabs
explanation: Docusign accepts a wide variety of document types including PDF, DOCX, RTF and PNG, so the files can be sent as they are with the correct fileExtension.
whyNotOthers: D is right. The trap is A: PDF is common, but not the only accepted type. B adds manual template work, and C drops robust anchor placement for no reason.

optionExplanations.A: Docusign accepts PDF, DOCX, RTF, PNG and more; conversion is unnecessary.
optionExplanations.B: This turns each one-off document into a template and adds manual work.
optionExplanations.C: Anchor tabs locate text in the document; there is no PDF-only rule, and fixed positions are less robust.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. Docusign accepts many file types, including DOCX, so no conversion service is needed.

decode.needs: Direct documents with DOCX, fileExtension docx
clues: Word files, conversion service -> unnecessary, DOCX is accepted
send next week -> simplest working approach
anchor text for signature lines -> keep anchor tabs

concept.title: Accepted document types
concept.line: Docusign accepts PDF, DOCX, RTF, PNG and others; set fileExtension so the file is converted on upload.

stem: What does the envelope status delivered mean?

options.text: At least one recipient has been sent an email with a link
All recipients have signed and the envelope is being finalised
All recipients have viewed the documents
The envelope has been completed by all recipients

answerText: All recipients have viewed the documents
explanation: Sent means at least one recipient got the link; delivered means all recipients have viewed; signed is temporary; completed ends the lifecycle.
whyNotOthers: C is right. The trap is A: it is the definition of sent. B and D are later statuses.

optionExplanations.A: That is the sent status.
optionExplanations.B: Signed is a temporary processing state before completed.
optionExplanations.C: Correct. Delivered means all recipients have viewed the documents.
optionExplanations.D: That is completed.

concept.title: Envelope lifecycle statuses
concept.line: created (draft) -> sent -> delivered (all viewed) -> signed (temporary) -> completed; voided and declined end it early.

topic: Replacing a document in an in-process envelope
stem: Ashby Construction sent a subcontract for signature this morning. Before anyone has signed, the project manager notices that the payment schedule attached as document 2 has an outdated rate. Legal wants to keep the same envelope, its recipients and its history, and simply swap in the corrected schedule. The integration already stores the envelope ID. The subcontractor is working on a remote site. Which call should the integration make?

options.text: EnvelopeRecipientTabs:update for the subcontractor with the corrected rate in the payment schedule's text tab
EnvelopeDocuments:update for the envelope with documentId 2 and the corrected file
Envelopes:update with status voided, then create a new envelope with the corrected schedule
EnvelopeDocuments:delete for document 2, leaving the subcontractor to sign without a payment schedule

answerText: EnvelopeDocuments:update for the envelope with documentId 2 and the corrected file
explanation: The in-process envelope can be modified with EnvelopeDocuments:update, specifying the documentId, to replace or add a document while keeping the envelope.
whyNotOthers: B is right. The trap is A: updating tabs is a valid in-process change, but the wrong rate is in the document content. C discards the envelope, and D removes the document entirely.

optionExplanations.A: Tabs are fields placed on documents; the rate is printed in the document itself, which must be replaced.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. EnvelopeDocuments:update adds or replaces a document in an in-process envelope.
optionExplanations.C: Voiding ends this envelope; legal wants to keep it.
optionExplanations.D: Deleting removes the schedule without providing the corrected one.

decode.needs: EnvelopeDocuments:update on the sent envelope
clues: before anyone has signed -> in-process envelope can still be modified
keep the same envelope and history -> no void
swap in the corrected schedule -> replace document 2
remote site -> red herring

concept.title: Modifying in-process documents
concept.line: EnvelopeDocuments:update adds or replaces documents in an in-process envelope; EnvelopeDocuments:delete removes them.

stem: Before calling EnvelopeRecipientTabs:update to change a recipient's existing fields, what must the app obtain?

options.text: The documentId of each document, from EnvelopeDocuments:list
A lock token from EnvelopeLocks:create for every tab update
The anchorString used when the tab was created
The tabId of each tab to change, from EnvelopeRecipientTabs:list

answerText: The tabId of each tab to change, from EnvelopeRecipientTabs:list
explanation: The course steps are: list the recipient's tabs, store the tabId of each tab to update, then PUT the entire tab objects with the changes.
whyNotOthers: D is right. The trap is B: locking is used when editing an in-process envelope, but the update itself is keyed by tabId. A and C identify other things.

optionExplanations.A: documentId identifies documents; tabs are updated by tabId.
optionExplanations.B: Locks are optional while editing; they are not the input the update needs.
optionExplanations.C: Existing tabs are identified by tabId, not anchors.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. List the recipient's tabs, store each tabId, then PUT the full tab objects with changes.

concept.title: Updating tabs needs tabId
concept.line: Call EnvelopeRecipientTabs:list for tabIds, then update with the full tab objects.
